options.rationale: Those are physical money.

stem: In its basic form, a blockchain is best described as…

options.content: an unalterable, time-stamped ledger
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: a central bank's private customer database
options.rationale: Blockchains are shared across many computers.

options.content: a cable network that links banks together
options.rationale: A blockchain is a record, not hardware.

options.content: a phone app for buying airtime
options.rationale: That is a mobile-money or shop app.

explanation: A blockchain is a digital ledger: a time-stamped series of records that cannot be altered.

stem: Why does each block in a blockchain store the hash of the previous block?

options.content: To encrypt the transactions so that nobody can read them
options.rationale: Linking hashes are not used to hide data.

options.content: To link the blocks, so any change to an earlier block is detected
options.rationale: Correct: altering a block changes its hash and breaks the link.

options.content: To record the time at which the block was created
options.rationale: That is the timestamp.

options.content: To store the users' passwords safely
options.rationale: Blocks do not hold passwords.

explanation: Each block carries the previous block's hash. Changing an old block changes its hash, so the next block's stored value no longer matches.

stem: Where are copies of a blockchain kept?

options.content: On a single central server
options.rationale: There is no single central copy.

options.content: On many computers (nodes) in the network
options.rationale: Correct: the ledger is shared.

options.content: Only on the buyer's phone
options.rationale: Every node holds a copy.

options.content: On the DNS servers of the internet
options.rationale: DNS servers do not hold blockchains.

explanation: Every node holds its own copy of the blockchain, so no single copy can be secretly changed.

stem: Chipo sent cryptocurrency to the wrong wallet by mistake. Why can the transaction not simply be deleted from the blockchain?

options.content: The transaction is encrypted with her private key
options.rationale: Encryption does not prevent deletion; the design of the ledger does.

options.content: Only a central bank can delete transactions
options.rationale: Cryptocurrencies have no central bank.

options.content: Blockchain records cannot be altered once added
options.rationale: Correct: a correction must be a new transaction.

options.content: Deleted transactions are restored from bookmarks
options.rationale: Bookmarks are a browser feature.

explanation: Records in a blockchain cannot be changed or removed; the receiver would have to send the amount back in a new transaction.
hints: Think about what makes a blockchain trustworthy.

stem: Which is a **drawback** of using a cryptocurrency?

options.content: Transfers can be made at any time of day
options.rationale: That is a benefit.

options.content: Every transaction is recorded permanently
options.rationale: That is the point of the ledger, usually seen as a benefit.

options.content: Its value can rise and fall sharply
options.rationale: Correct: values can be very volatile.

options.content: No physical notes need to be printed
options.rationale: That is a feature, not a drawback.

explanation: Drawbacks include volatile value, loss if wallet keys are lost or stolen, use in crime and, for some, high energy use.
hints: Three options are features or benefits.

explanation: False. Cryptocurrencies are not controlled by a central bank; their transactions are verified by the network of nodes.

explanation: Nodes verify; transactions go into a block; every node updates its copy.

stem: A blockchain has 9 blocks, numbered 1 to 9. An attacker changes a transaction in block 6. Each block stores the hash of the previous block. Including block 6, how many blocks would the attacker have to rewrite to make the chain consistent again?
explanation: Block 6 and every block after it (6, 7, 8, 9): 4 blocks, on most of the nodes at once, which is practically impossible.
workedSolution:
1. Changing block 6 changes its hash, so block 7's stored "previous hash" no longer matches.
2. Rewriting block 7 changes its hash, breaking block 8, and so on to block 9.
3. Blocks 6 to 9: $9 - 6 + 1 = 4$.
hints: Changing block 6 changes its hash. Which block stores that hash?
That block's hash then changes too…

explanation: Cryptocurrency transactions are recorded in a blockchain.

stem: Explain what is meant by a digital currency and how it is used. [2]

points.description: It exists only electronically (no physical notes or coins)
It is used by transferring amounts as data between digital accounts/wallets, e.g. to pay for goods or send money

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A digital currency only exists in electronic form. It is used by transferring amounts as data from one digital wallet or account to another to pay for goods or send money.

hints: What is missing compared with ordinary money? How is it moved?

stem: Explain how a blockchain is used to track digital currency transactions. [4]

points.description: Each new transaction is verified by the nodes in the network
Verified transactions are stored in a block that is time-stamped
Each block holds the previous block's hash, linking the blocks into a chain (so changes are detected)
Every node holds a copy of the chain and the records cannot be altered

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: When a transaction is made, nodes in the network verify it. It is placed in a time-stamped block that also stores the hash of the previous block, so the blocks form a chain. The new block is added to every node's copy. Because the blocks are linked and copies are everywhere, records cannot be altered, so the full history of transactions can be traced.

explanation: Verify, block, timestamp, link, copies, unalterable.
hints: Mention blocks, timestamps, links and copies.

stem: A craft co-operative in Masvingo is considering accepting a cryptocurrency for online sales to overseas customers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which statement about the cryptocurrency is correct?

options.content: It is issued as banknotes
options.rationale: It has no physical form.

options.content: It is controlled by one bank
options.rationale: Cryptocurrencies have no central authority.

options.content: Its transactions can be edited later
options.rationale: Records cannot be altered.

options.content: It exists only in electronic form
options.rationale: Correct.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain why a customer could not later change the record of a payment to the co-operative.

points.description: The payment is stored in a time-stamped block in the blockchain
The next block stores this block's hash, so changing it would break the chain / be detected
Copies are held on many nodes, which would reject an altered copy

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The payment is in a time-stamped block. Changing it would change its hash, which no longer matches the value stored in the next block, and the many other copies held by nodes would show the change, so it would be rejected.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Give **one** benefit and **one** drawback for the co-operative.

points.description: Benefit: fast international payments at any time / no need for the customer to have a local bank account
Drawback: value can fall sharply / keys can be lost or stolen / not all customers use it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Overseas customers can pay quickly at any time, but the value of the money received could fall sharply before it is spent.

explanation: Digital currency exists only electronically; blockchain records are linked, time-stamped and copied, so cannot be altered.
hints: What makes changing an old record detectable?
Benefits and drawbacks for a small business.

stem: What happens to a new transaction **before** it is added to a block in the blockchain?

options.content: It is printed and signed at a bank
options.rationale: There is no paper record.

options.content: It is sent to a DNS server for approval
options.rationale: DNS servers have no role in blockchains.

options.content: It is deleted from the payer's wallet
options.rationale: Only a verified, recorded transaction changes balances.

options.content: It is verified by nodes in the network
options.rationale: Correct: nodes check it is valid, e.g. that the payer has enough to spend.

explanation: Nodes verify a transaction (for example, that the payer has enough to spend) before it is placed in a time-stamped block.
